_readme: ONE DEFECT SITE PER TASK, consumed by `node scripts/b12-spec.mjs write`. Everything
else about a task — parent, fileScope, predicate, stratum — lives in corpus-plan.json
`find` must appear EXACTLY ONCE in the scoped file; the writer refuses on zero and on
more than one, because a replacement landing twice would leave the fileScope claiming
one edit while the tree carries two.
SELF-CONTAINED IS THE PROPERTY THAT MATTERS. A defect whose fix requires touching a
file outside the declared fileScope makes scope confinement unsatisfiable, and the
observation voids for a reason the author planted. That is why both sites below are
INTERNAL helpers: dropping the nullable half of an exported signature would push the
error out to callers in other files.
`symptom` says what BROKE and never what to change. It is pasted into prompt.md above
a fixed instruction to stay in scope and leave the tests alone.
The two entries here are already authored and published as annotated tags; the writer
skips a task whose spec dir exists rather than rewriting it. They are kept as the

tylmsopt.symptom:
`npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` is failing in `src/lms.ts`. A helper that reports a
numeric field from an `lms` JSON row is declared to always produce a number, but the row
it reads may simply not carry that field.

typarseblk.symptom:
`npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` is failing in `src/parse.ts`. The helper that locates a
closing fence on its own line is declared to always find one, and a segment with no such
line has nothing to report.

tychkparse.find: function firstLineIn(stack: string, file: string | null): number | null {
tychkparse.replace: function firstLineIn(stack: string, file: string | null): number {
tychkparse.symptom:
`npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` is failing in `src/checks/parsers.ts`. The helper that
pulls a line number out of a stack trace is declared to always find one — but it is handed
a nullable file, and a stack that never mentions that file has no line to give.
